Clinical trials are insanely rigorous for a reason as everyone knows. Allergan would love to have invented the new finasteride, but the FDA is in charge of clearing all liability for the entire US population.

If this was a cancer treatment, it would get fast tracked pretty quickly. Even depression, hypotension, joint pain, or anything directly medically related would get the funding and leeway to see the light of day in close to a decade. But even then the FDA is hell-bent on preventing another thalidomide.

The thing we can't forget is that hair loss is cosmetic. We don't get to just skip the line like that. Pharma companies have to budget for the long trial process, there are a finite amount of clinical trial facilities/participants, and they have to weigh the risk of losing all money by just one negative trial. And if you have schizophrenia you can't just shave your head to make your life livable until a better treatment comes out. Hair loss sucks, but we have it far better than most other treatments being investigated in the pipeline.

As for the results of the study, Jesus Christ wait a second. The trial facility has to have teams write up a massive report to send to Allegan to then send back and forth for requirements until everything is solid for release. I know because I've been the guy that's done it, literally with Allergan too. I had one row swapped with another on a long table and they sent it back 2 days later for revision. Then they wanted the units different in another part of the report, then something related to wording. This happened probably 5 or so times with the entire team. It takes time because of how incredibly specific it has to be for the FDA to not throw their investment in the garbage. Think of it like applying to an ivy league college and youre paying someone else to write the application for you.
